tagline: Into the gorge the Cherokee named for the noonday sun.
intro: From the old quarry town of Marble the byway follows US 74 east through Andrews, a railroad town, and Topton, and down into the Nantahala Gorge. River and highway run the gorge together, with the excursion railroad beside them, and come out at Wesser, where the Nantahala goes into Fontana Lake. The last miles cross to Bryson City on the Tuckasegee.

In 1839 the way through the gorge was a rough path, part of the Trail of Tears, as the Cherokee were driven west out of these mountains. Their name for the place means Land of the Noonday Sun. In parts of the gorge the sun reaches the ground only when it stands straight overhead.

moments.title: Marble
moments.text: The quarries here cut Regal Blue and Confederate Gray marble for headstones in nine states and for a county courthouse built of nothing else, and every one of them has filled with water.

moments.title: Wesser
moments.text: The take-out for the gorge's eight miles of Class II and III rapids, just above Wesser Falls, where the river pitches off at about 45 degrees on its way into Fontana Lake.

moments.title: Bryson City
moments.text: The Swain County seat sits on the Tuckasegee a little downstream from Kituwa, the village the Cherokee held to be their oldest, and keeps monuments to Tsali and Yonaguska.
